features.name: Models-as-a-Service (MaaS) core: access model and token mechanism

timeline.detail: Introduced as Technology Preview. Governance was tier-based: OpenShift group membership selected a single highest-priority tier controlling model access, request limits, and token quotas. Authentication used a MaaS-issued, service-account-backed token (Authorization: Bearer <token>).

Reached GA. Tiers replaced by subscriptions and dedicated CRs (MaaSSubscription, MaaSAuthPolicy, MaaSModelRef). Authentication changed to subscription-bound API keys with the sk-oai- prefix (one-hour temporary or managed with expiration/revocation). Credential/policy/storage/governance NOT backward compatible with 3.3 -- amber TP-to-GA migration break, not a red regression of an already-GA service.

GA core expanded: external OIDC authentication for MaaS reaches GA (map OIDC group claims to subscriptions, issue API keys without requiring OpenShift accounts, coexists with OpenShift-group auth). OpenAI-compatible body-based model routing reaches GA (drop-in with openai/LangChain/LlamaIndex/OpenWebUI; legacy path-based routing still supported). Subscriptions + Authorization policy pages merge into one MaaS governance page (Settings -> MaaS governance).
Gateway API replacing OpenShift Routes, kube-rbac-proxy replacing oauth-proxy -- core architecture shift. Custom workbench images built against oauth-proxy require rebuilding.

Direct authentication with an external OIDC provider through the Gateway API, configured via the GatewayConfig CR, reaches GA. This is a platform authentication feature, not MaaS-specific, though MaaS traffic flows through the same Gateway -- easy to conflate with MaaS-specific external OIDC, but distinct.
No maturity change; unchanged platform capability. (Distinct sub-feature: MaaS-specific external OIDC user authentication moved TP->GA in 3.5 -- see maas-external-oidc.)
Technology Preview. Distinct from the platform-wide Gateway OIDC capability.

TP -> GA in 3.5. Administrators integrate an external OIDC identity provider, map OIDC group claims to MaaS subscriptions, and issue API keys scoped to OIDC group memberships -- without requiring OpenShift accounts.

features.name: Llama Stack / OGX (Open GenAI Stack) core: RAG, agentic workflows, vector DB integration

timeline.detail: Introduced as Technology Preview (distribution ~0.2.22-class). Remote inference, built-in embeddings, vector DB operations, TrustyAI safety/eval integration.
PostgreSQL Operator became a hard requirement. Distribution 0.3.5. HA configuration and custom embeddings added as TP sub-features.
Distribution 0.4.2. Multi-architecture Operator support became default. OpenAI-compatible citation annotations added as TP.

Llama Stack Operator remains Technology Preview in the formal 3.4 support matrix (0.9.0, TP on x86_64/Arm/Power, unavailable on IBM Z). Responses API alignment, connectors, Conversations API, and FAISS additions do not promote the operator itself to GA.

Renamed to OGX at 3.5 EA1 (breaking manual migration: remove Llama Stack Operator, create new OGXServer resources; API group llamastack.io->ogx.io; v1alpha1->v1beta1; kind LlamaStackDistribution->OGXServer; activation field spec.components.llamastackoperator.managementState->spec.components.ogx.managementState). At 3.5 GA: Supported Configurations lists OGX Operator 0.11.0 / OGX 1.1.2 as GA on x86_64, Arm, IBM Power, while the current OGX product guide labels the OpenShift AI integration Technology Preview, and individual APIs/providers range GA/TP/DP (Responses API is GA; most others TP/DP). State component, integration, and per-API/provider maturity as separate layers -- never collapse into one label.

Scope substantially widened: embedded directly into AI Pipelines, workbenches, the Kubeflow SDK, Kubeflow Trainer, and AI Hub. Training jobs run through a pipeline or SDK are tracked by a dedicated per-project MLflow server -- closes the previously documented MLflow-to-Kubeflow-Trainer gap. Automated Red Teaming (Garak) separately reaches GA (see automated-red-teaming). Dashboard comparison, MCP server, thresholds, and Kueue-routed scheduling remain TP.

integration_notes.title: Guardrails x MaaS / OGX / MCP Gateway: the 3.5 integration paths are distinct
integration_notes.detail: FMS-Guardrails retains a documented OGX integration path via the trustyai_fms external provider, but FMS Guardrails is formally deprecated in 3.5 and Red Hat directs new deployments to NeMo Guardrails. The current 3.5 OGX security guide documents a native NeMo Guardrails integration as the recommended production guardrails path -- this should NOT be generalized into a MaaS-specific integration; no equivalent MaaS-native NeMo control-plane feature is documented. The Gen AI Playground guardrails experience differs by milestone (EA1: NeMo-powered; GA Technology Preview chapter: 'basic guardrails' sourced from OGX, limited to llm_input/llm_output, tool-level guardrails excluded -- follow GA documentation for current-state wording). Separately, NeMo Guardrails x MCP Gateway (introduced 3.5 EA2) remains Technology Preview and enforces guardrails on agent tool calls at the gateway layer, requiring the MCP Gateway Operator as an external prerequisite.

integration_notes.title: Model Registry to MaaS: no re-registration required, but the connection point is the deployment, not the registry entry
integration_notes.detail: Documented path: Model Registry -> deployment through the standard InferenceService flow -> enabling the model as an available AI asset/service from the deployment interface (a Developer Preview integration in 3.3/3.4, distinct from MaaS core which is GA). No separate re-registration step is required, but the connection point is one step removed from where a user might expect it. No 3.5 release-note entry found changing this relationship.

integration_notes.title: MLflow to Kubeflow Trainer v2: confirmed gap at 3.4, confirmed closed at 3.5 GA
integration_notes.detail: At 3.4, automatic MLflow SDK configuration was scoped to workbenches only (opendatahub.io/mlflow-instance annotation); no equivalent auto-attach mechanism was found for Kubeflow Trainer v2 TrainJobs -- a documented gap. At 3.5 GA, Red Hat's own release notes state MLflow tracking is embedded directly into AI Pipelines, workbenches, the Kubeflow SDK, Kubeflow Trainer, and AI Hub, and that training jobs run through a pipeline or SDK are automatically tracked by a dedicated MLflow server instance -- a direct, dated closure of the gap. Training Hub's Ray integration (SFT/OSFT/LoRA/GRPO) is documented separately without an explicit MLflow auto-attach statement for Ray-submitted jobs specifically -- re-verify independently before assuming identical behavior to the Kubeflow Trainer path.

integration_notes.title: Feature Store to AutoML/AutoRAG: appears isolated -- inferred from documentation silence, not confirmed
integration_notes.detail: AutoRAG's documented prerequisites (an OGX instance, a remote Milvus vector database -- inline Milvus explicitly not supported -- and S3-compatible document storage) never mention Feature Store, in the prerequisites, the introduction blog post, or interactive demo materials. AutoRAG's 3.5 enhancements (CPU-only support, multilingual support, structural contextualization) contain no documented Feature Store dependency. This is an absence of evidence after a renewed search, not confirmation no integration exists -- a later release could connect them without release-note language using these exact terms. Adjacent: a documented 3.4 bug (RHOAIENG-64768) causes AutoML/AutoRAG default pipelines to hang on ImagePullBackOff due to unavailable image digests; no 3.5 resolved-issues entry confirming a fix was located -- treat as open until re-verified against the current z-stream.

integration_notes.title: EvalHub x MLflow: confirmed integration (EvalCard generation)
integration_notes.detail: EvalCard generation, new at 3.5 GA, is a directly documented integration: when an evaluation job request specifies an MLflow experiment (or OCI export configuration), EvalHub's runtime automatically generates a schema-validated JSON EvalCard capturing metadata, results, provenance, and pass/fail outcomes, storing it as an MLflow run artifact (or OCI artifact). EvalHub's overall 3.5 support label remains subject to the GA-vs-TP source conflict documented for the evalhub feature.

operational_notes.detail: 3.0 and 3.2 offered no upgrade path from 2.x at all -- new installs only. 3.3.2 specifically (not 3.3.0/3.3.1) is the first 3.x release supporting migration from 2.x, and only from 2.25.4 or later -- a precise version gate. This is a migration with significant component changes, not zero-downtime: requires a proactive support case, complete backup, prerequisite checks, and the rhai-cli migration assessment process. Unconverted ModelMesh/KServe Serverless models return HTTP 503 immediately after upgrade with no grace period; OGX (Llama Stack) data is permanently lost during migration unless backed up beforehand, with no automated migration path. Custom workbench images built against oauth-proxy must be rebuilt for kube-rbac-proxy or they fail with redirect loops. RHOAI 3.3 requires OpenShift 4.19.9 specifically. Release cadence: EA1 (1 month, unsupported) -> EA2 -> GA (7 months full support); EUS releases add 11 more months on top; one EUS release per three GA releases.

At 3.5 GA, a dedicated migration guide ('Assess and plan for migration from 2.25.9+ to 3.5') ships using rhai-cli, covering side-by-side and in-place approaches, Kueue management-state prerequisites, and component-specific rhai-cli migrate actions for Kueue/RHBOK, AI Pipelines, Model Serving, Workbenches, TrustyAI, Training, Llama Stack/OGX, and Ray. After upgrading, move off the support-required-upgrade-3.5 channel onto stable-3.5 / stable-3.x / eus-3.5 per lifecycle needs. New 3.5-specific item: anyone who configured llm-d flow control during the 3.4 TP window must update the API group, metrics prefix, and saturation-detector configuration path before/during the 3.5 upgrade.

Architecture support is per-component, not per-product-label: a 3.5 GA product on a supported OpenShift architecture does not imply every AI component is GA there. The 3.5 release notes announce IBM Power support for OGX, KubeRay, MLflow, AutoML, AutoRAG, the GenAI playground, and milvus-lite, but the current matrix is narrower: OGX is GA on Power; KubeRay/MLflow/AutoML are TP; AutoRAG is not listed on Power at all -- treated as source conflicts, matrix governs. The Llama Stack/OGX Operator remains unavailable on IBM Z. NeMo Guardrails has a direct IBM Z source conflict (announced vs. matrix absence). vLLM CPU ServingRuntime on IBM Z/Power is permanently restricted to standard deployment mode only. New at 3.5: llm-d's cross-Kubernetes expansion (GA on AKS/CKS, TP on EKS) is a Kubernetes-platform dimension layered on top of, not a replacement for, the existing hardware-architecture dimension; the llm-d tokenizer's new dedicated-amd64-node requirement is new at 3.5 (previously ran with the EndpointPicker on amd64 or ARM).

Known issue RHOAIENG-54101 (discovered 3.4 EA1): on IBM Z, a model deployed from Model Registry does not appear under the registry's own Deployments tab; workaround is to manage it from the global Deployments page. No 3.5 resolved-issues entry confirming a fix was located -- recheck against the current z-stream.

Starting with 3.5, RStudio Server and CUDA - RStudio Server workbench images are removed outright (not merely deprecated) due to AGPL licensing-compliance issues in bundled packages/binaries. Already-running RStudio workbenches keep operating post-upgrade, but new ones cannot be created and stopped ones cannot be restarted from the dashboard. RStudio remains available (supported) on 2.25 (EOL 5 Oct 2026) and 3.3 (EOL 26 Apr 2027) only. Unsupported self-build recipes exist for 3.5+. This is a compliance-driven removal, not a product-direction one -- flag distinctly from the vLLM/OGX/MaaS architectural changes when advising R-workflow customers.

LM-Eval (LMEvalJob CRD + UI) is deprecated at 3.5, will be removed in a future release; migrate to EvalHub (now including LM Evaluation Harness support). The OGX Evaluation REST API and its providers were deprecated AND removed from the OGX Operator in the same 3.5 EA1 milestone -- an unusually fast deprecation-to-removal cycle. The Safety and Shields APIs/providers in OGX were deprecated at 3.5 EA1. Combined with the FMS Guardrails deprecation, this is a deliberate, multi-pronged consolidation of safety/evaluation tooling onto NeMo Guardrails and EvalHub respectively.

Starting with 3.4, Red Hat Connectivity Link (RHCL) is included in Red Hat AI SKUs for Models-as-a-Service use cases only; for all other RHOAI components RHCL is not included -- when MaaS is enabled, RHCL is deployed via the Kuadrant Operator. No change at 3.5. The Seldon alibi-detect and alibi-explain libraries ship inside the certified Seldon MLServer runtime but are licensed under Business Source License 1.1; Red Hat explicitly states they are 'not tested, verified, or supported' as part of that certified runtime and recommends against production use -- a library physically present in a supported runtime but carved out of the support boundary entirely. Unchanged at 3.5.

Llama Stack renamed to OGX (Open GenAI Stack) at 3.5 EA1 -- see ogx-core and the Llama Stack -> OGX rename deprecation-timeline entry for the full breaking-change detail. Data Science Pipelines renamed to AI Pipelines at 3.0 (datasciencepipelines component -> aipipelines in the DataScienceCluster CR). A complete rename audit across all 2.x/3.x release notes remains out of scope; no additional rename beyond OGX was identified for the 3.5 cycle in the sources reviewed.

RHOAI has its own documented API support-tier policy (separate from the generic OpenShift Container Platform API tier system), present in every version 3.0 through 3.5: APIs are stable within a major release for a minimum of nine months from the announcement of deprecation; APIs may be deprecated and removed within a major release; APIs may have a longer deprecation window than the minimum. The actual per-endpoint tier table is gated behind a Red Hat customer portal subscription login and could not be retrieved for this registry -- pull it directly from the portal for endpoint-level planning. The public, granular OGX per-endpoint/provider table (ogx_provider_table in this registry) is useful for OGX planning specifically but is not the same as the gated cross-product tier table.
